title: MobX
description: Model observable state with MobX, derive values with computed, and react with the observer HOC.

data.text: MobX makes state observable and re-renders any React component that reads it. Instead of dispatching actions, you mutate observables directly and let computed values and reactions update automatically.

data.caption: src/stores/todoStore.ts

data.title: makeObservable needs annotations
data.text: `makeObservable(this)` only works when you pass annotation maps or use decorators. Use `makeAutoObservable(this)` (as above) or supply `{ todos: observable, add: action, visibleTodos: computed }` explicitly.

data.caption: observer components re-render on observable reads

data.text: `observer` wraps the component so reads are tracked and re-renders are automatic. Values that never touch an observable (local `useState` here) keep behaving like normal React state.

terms.definition: A value MobX tracks for reads and changes.
A function that changes observables; batching them keeps derivations consistent.
A cached value derived from observables that recomputes only when its inputs change.
A HOC that subscribes a React component to the observables it reads.

items.question: Is MobX still a reasonable choice?
items.answer: Yes, especially for complex domain models where derived data is common. It is less popular than Redux or Zustand in new React apps, but it remains powerful and is widely used in Vue-like reactive architectures.

items.question: Why wrap async updates in runInAction?
items.answer: MobX enforces that observables change inside actions. After an await you are outside the action, so runInAction re-establishes the batching context.

data.title: What interviewers look for
data.text: Contrast MobX's transparent reactivity (you mutate and the UI follows) with Redux's explicit immutability and action log. Mention `runInAction` as the async gotcha.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: makeAutoObservable turns class fields into observables and methods into actions.
observer components re-render only for the observables they read.
data.takeaway: MobX is the counter-example to Redux: mutable, automatic, and implicit — know both sides.
